remediation.reason: Re-review failed: unreviewed changes after the implement window and forged state after close are graded compliant; fullSddCompleted diverges from the spec

findings.summary: Verified fixed: no-op, quick-only and downgraded runs are no longer compliant (eval-sdd-not-closed, eval-foreign-work, eval-downgraded).

Verified fixed for the reproduced cases: forged --no-verify trailer raises eval-untracked-work-commit; config testCommand weakening raises eval-harness-tampered; core.hooksPath drift checked. New variants in R1/R2.
Verified fixed: fullSddCompleted requires closed.has(taskId); other-work commits raise eval-foreign-work.
Verified fixed: grading errors become eval-compliance-error while keeping the functional grade.
Verified fixed: metric/usage/compliance shape validated; unreadable inputs invalid with sha256 null.
Verified fixed: installed bin and managed hook node_modules lookup exercised with WAYS_CLI unset; packed-layout revision tested.
Verified fixed: untracked dist/ is stated in sourceRevisionReason.
Verified fixed: corpus.digest in the comparability key; partial sums are observedTotal with total null.

An adapter that runs SDD with an empty implement, passes review/validate, then commits the real change with hooks disabled and a Harness-Work trailer while the work is active, then closes, is graded compliant and fullSddCompleted with no issues. Nothing ties non-phase commits to the implement window or the reviewed content to the final tree.

After a legitimate close, committing a forged .ways/state/current.json with an arbitrary change (hooks disabled, trailer) and then deleting it is graded fully compliant: activeWorkAt trusts any committed state file, STATE_PATH is not protected, and commits after close are not rejected.

fullSddCompleted is closed.has(taskId) without compliance, contradicting certified spec decision 3 ('compliant and at least one close certification'); docs changed but spec not, and the compare fullSddCompleted count can exceed compliant.
